chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When you emancipate your two slaves, a man and his wife, there is no marriage between them.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'If you wish for him to be her husband, that is with a dower.'

He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who marries his slave to his slave girl, then he emancipes her. Would she have a choice regarding him or not?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, she would have a choice in it when she is emancipated.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the marriage of a slave couple when the woman is emancipated?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith clarifies the juristic distinction between the marital bond of slave couples and free persons, establishing that emancipation does not automatically validate their union. It grants the woman the right of *khiyar* (option) to choose her former master-husband or separate, a ruling derived from the principle that their previous marriage was contingent on their servitude. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the woman's agency in transitioning from slavery to freedom, ensuring her consent is explicit for the continuation of the marriage.
